summary: SSE: lingered TCP socket results in interleaved token fragments and missing final event on client reconnect
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that after a short mobile network switch the SSE stream resumes but the final 'end' event is missing and some token fragments are interleaved/duplicated. The behaviour is repeatable from the customer's environment when they trigger a cellular->wifi handoff. Impact: Produces incomplete outputs to end users and causes client-side reassembly failures; NoteFlow reported user-visible truncation in 3 of 10 resumed sessions and data loss for the last paragraph in many cases.

Observed behaviour: When client reconnects following a transient socket drop, the resumed stream sometimes contains duplicated prefix tokens, interleaved heartbeat frames, and the terminal 'event: done' or final JSON marker is not received. Client SDK shows partial last-choice and then the connection closes. Server traces show the backend had emitted the final marker.

Expected behaviour: Resume should stitch prior partials and deliver the final marker exactly once. No duplication of in-flight fragments and no suppression of end-event.

Context/notes: Customer uses Redwood Dedicated with reserved pool in us-east. They use our Node.js client SDK on mobile webview that falls back to SSE. Traffic flows through customer's corp Envoy + our api-gateway + internal edge Envoy. They have occasional short-lived path migrations (TCP 4-tuple change).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start a long streaming generation (>10s) from NoteFlow mobile webview using Node SDK and SSE.
2) During generation, trigger network handoff (cellular -> wifi) to force local socket migration.
3) Client attempts SSE reconnect using last resume token.
4) Observe stream fragments delivered to client and whether final 'done' event arrives.

Repro rate observed by customer: approx 30% when handoff occurs under their mobile carrier. Internal repro: 2/20 with simulated socket short-close and Envoy reuse in lab cluster.
logs_and_artifacts:
Customer-provided logs: trace_id=nf-20260309-6a3b, client-log excerpt: 'resume: token=eyJr...; received chunk: "...partial sentence A"; then "heartbeat"; then "...partial sentence B"; connection close with no done'.
Server side: request_id=req-8c12, backend worker log shows 'emitted final_event done for req-8c12 at 2026-03-09T16:42:12Z'.
Edge traces: envoy-conn-47 lingered FIN_WAIT for 35s and then a RST was observed from intermediate proxy. See attached packet capture snippet at s3://redwood-support/noteflow/sup-834560/pktcap.pcap (customer shared).
Related live dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/streaming/resume?trace=req-8c12
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Intermediate proxy (customer Envoy + our edge Envoy) is reusing connections and a lingering TCP FIN/RST race causes fragments from two different upstream workers to be interleaved at the mux layer, leading to parser confusion on the client.
Hypothesis 2: Our API-gateway's resume token mapping lookup returned a stale in-memory session due to connection pooling and reassigns stream fragments to a new response channel without clearing prior in-flight buffer.
Initial findings: Reproduced partial duplication with lab setup when enabling SO_LINGER on server socket and enabling HTTP/1.1 connection reuse across Envoy. Packet capture shows two overlapping TCP segments for same stream id with different sequence numbers arriving to client.
Related PR that may be relevant: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/582
Linked Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C05SUPPORT/p164693 (internal discussion with SRE).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Support (Ava Chen): Acknowledged with customer, asked for pktcap and last-resume-token. Customer supplied pcap and session logs.

2026-03-10 - SRE (Diego Morales): Verified edge envoy showed FIN linger ~35s and then RST during path migration. Confirmed backend logged 'final_event' before RST. Beginning deeper packet-level analysis.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Priya Patel): Ran reproduce in staging with SO_LINGER toggled. Observed interleaved fragments when upstream closed with linger and envoy connection pooling enabled. Suspect mux layer not atomically swapping stream buffers on resume mapping.
2026-03-11 - Customer (NoteFlow eng): Provided repeatable repro plan and consented to enabling additional logging on their dedicated pool for a short window. Asked for ETA on workaround.

2026-03-12 - Support (Diego Morales): Applied temporary mitigation: disabled keepalive-reuse on edge envoy for NoteFlow's customer pool; requested customer to validate. Customer confirmed 8/8 handoffs succeeded without truncation during 2-hour window.
2026-03-12 - Eng (Priya Patel): Opening a follow-up internal task to harden resume atomicity in mux layer and add defensive checks for duplicate-segment detection. See INT-34012 for internal rollout.
resolution:
Workaround applied: disabled connection reuse for the customer's dedicated pool at the edge Envoy which mitigated the issue during validation window. Root cause: race at mux/resume token mapping when a lingered socket produced overlapping segments after path migration; envoy reuse surfaced duplicate/interleaved fragments to the client.
Permanent fix plan: Engineering to implement atomic swap and duplicate-segment guard in serving runtime, add detection/metrics to Console, and add a conservative default for keepalive/connection-reuse around resume windows. Target PR queued: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/590.
Follow-ups: INT-34012 (ensure canary rollout), add a Confluence runbook for SSE resume debug (CONFLUENCE-STREAM-RESUME-RUNBOOK).
